about: PROPOSED, UNSIGNED. Six Proofline tasks, XC-91 to XC-96, for an opt-in matrix: a .NET / C# SDK harness run locally against testnet fixtures, rows on opt-in (XC-91); a passive unpaid 402-challenge check for merchants and paid APIs that accepted (XC-92); one row format with Environment, passed/run counts, version, release alignment, date and evidence, and a compact docs/MATRIX.md (XC-93); self-serve tooling so a project can run the suite on itself and send its row (XC-94); attribution and credit: the badge, CC BY 4.0 for public results, provenance in every run, NOTICE and CITATION.cff (XC-95); and the opt-in matrix itself: the form, schema and validating workflow to a PR, the Pages table, an example row, badges and weekly freshness (XC-96). Owner's go 2026-10-25T17:55Z, attribution 18:11Z, matrix rows 18:43Z, opt-in 18:53Z, freshness 18:57Z. Nothing here is binding and vv does not read this file. It becomes part of the contract only when the owner key signs it into proofline.json. Evidence is testnet-only, loopback-only or passive read-only; hosted facilitators are never called and nothing is paid. Estimated effort: 18-20 days.

not_contract_tasks.keys: Throwaway testnet keys are created on the owner's machine and live in X402C_KEYS outside the repository. They are never funded for these tasks. No spend, no mainnet.
not_contract_tasks.disclosure: A failing third-party row is reported to that project privately first (SECURITY.md). Until the window clears its row shows the failed count and 'under disclosure', with no per-check detail.
not_contract_tasks.contact: Outreach is private and outside these tasks: the list of projects asked is never committed. A project that accepts adds or updates its own row through the form or a pull request.

tasks.description: A merchant or paid API that publishes an x402 endpoint can be listed once it accepts (XC-96), with a row of type merchant-paid-api. tools/merchant_rows.py --run <slug> runs only for a slug that has a consented matrix/rows/<slug>.json of that type with a testnet endpoint; it refuses any other slug. It first reads the origin's robots.txt and stops with 'not run: robots' if automated access to that path is disallowed; otherwise it runs `x402conf resource --min-interval 5 --max-requests 3` on the testnet endpoint, which sends one unpaid GET and grades the 402 challenge (P1-P7, and P9 when the bazaar extension is present) against the spec. It never sends a payment header, never signs, never POSTs, never calls /verify, /settle or /supported on any host, and never pays. Requests to any one host are at least 5 s apart. An accepted row that offers mainnet only is live-not-run ('mainnet only, not run') and nothing is fetched. The bundle goes through tools/row_from_evidence.py with the row's consent issue, so the row, its counts and its badge come from committed evidence in the XC-93 format. No list of merchants is committed: the outreach list is private.

tasks.description: One row format for the matrix, generated from committed files and never typed by hand. docs/MATRIX.md is compact: a link to add or update a row at the top, a coverage summary of accepted projects (counts by type, chain, language and environment), the table of accepted projects with evidence (generated by tools/matrix_rows.py from matrix/rows/*.json, XC-96), one example row labelled 'Example (illustrative, not a real result)', and the suite's reference baseline (tools/compat_matrix.py, the stock example servers, marked as baseline and not listings). Every listed row has: Environment, one of testnet (run against a public testnet or devnet endpoint), devnet (run locally from source or fixtures, on loopback, with testnet or devnet ids), live-not-run (mainnet only, not exercised) or out-of-reach (hosted only, or nothing public to run against); the version or commit tested; the release alignment (XC-96); checks passed out of checks run (for example 42/48) and the failed count; the last run date linking the committed run.json; an 'add or update' link; and, in the baseline table, 'rerun / get listed' and 'missing check?' links. Failed checks appear as a count only: no check names, no narrative. There is no overall score, rank, ordering by result or 'certified' wording in the matrix's own text (headers and prose); a project's own name is not wording, so a project called, say, agent-score is listed under its name. The 'rerun / get listed' section gives the self-serve path (XC-94, XC-96). The 'missing check?' link goes to the check-proposal issue form and the governance for check proposals (XC-53). The XC-76 scoreboard can read the same fields; this task does not change its rules.

tasks.title: Run it yourself: the Action's evidence mode, an 'Add or update my row' issue form, and the path from a run to a matrix-row PR

deadline.from: signed into proofline.json and every depends_on task done

on_lapse: reassign to the next free agent

tasks.description: Any facilitator, SDK, merchant or vendor can run the suite on itself and send its details without waiting for me. (1) The existing Action (action.yml, used as `uses: atsp-protocol/x402-conformance@v<version>`) gains an evidence mode: inputs `evidence: true` and `row: <slug>` write the run as an evidence bundle (run.json as the probe wrote it, a README with the stack, version or commit, network and command, and SHA256SUMS), refuse a mainnet CAIP-2 id or a non-loopback facilitator URL through tools/evidence_guard.py, and upload the bundle with actions/upload-artifact. It runs against the vendor's own testnet or devnet endpoint or a local build started with `start`. (2) A GitHub issue form, 'Add or update my row' (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/matrix-row.yml, detailed in XC-96), collects the project's public details, the environments it offers, a testnet endpoint if any, the version, a public contact handle, the required consents, and optionally the run.json from an Action run. (3) tools/row_from_evidence.py turns that artifact (or a local run) into the files of one matrix row under evidence/, checks the hashes and the guard, and regenerates the row with tools/compat_matrix.py --write, so the vendor (or I) can open a PR that updates the row from committed evidence; the documented path is issue or Action run, then that PR, then CI regenerates and checks the row. A row is listed only with consent recorded in the issue or the PR. A 'live' environment is accepted as GET-only resource checks (x402conf resource) and is never a payment. (4) docs/RUN-IT-YOURSELF.md is a short quick start with the CLI (pip x402conf and npx x402conf-svm), the Action with evidence mode, and the MCP server, ending with how to get listed. Every command and workflow block in it is run by the docs-examples check (XC-27).

deadline.from: signed into proofline.json and every depends_on task done

tasks.description: Credit that travels with the results, without claiming more than the evidence shows. (1) Only a listed project (opt-in, XC-96) with committed evidence gets a badge, for its own README: tools/matrix_rows.py --write writes docs/site/badge/<slug>.svg, served by the Pages site, reading 'Tested with x402-conformance · Optitransfer' and the version tested, grey with 'stale' when the row is stale, and linking to the project's row on the Pages matrix. The reference baseline has no badge. docs/MATRIX.md and the Pages matrix give copy-paste Markdown and HTML for each row. The wording is descriptive only: never 'certified', 'x402 certified', 'compliant' or 'approved'. docs/BADGE.md gives the terms: only the official badge URL on the Pages site counts, the badge says a run exists and links to it, and it is not an endorsement. Embeds are counted only from the HTTP referrer in the Pages access data: no tracking pixel, no script, no cookie, no third-party analytics. (2) DATA-LICENSE puts the public matrix data and committed evidence (matrix/rows/*.json, docs/compat-matrix.json, docs/site/matrix/rows.json, docs/site/scoreboard.json and evidence/**) under CC BY 4.0 with the attribution line 'x402-conformance by Optitransfer' and a link to the repository. It covers public results only; any private research data and any future paid deep-testing output are out of its scope. docs/MATRIX.md carries the same note. (3) The code stays Apache-2.0; NOTICE credits Ryan Gillespie / Optitransfer. (4) Every results document the suite writes (Python results JSON and the TypeScript probe's run.json) has a provenance object: suite x402-conformance, the version, publisher Optitransfer, and the repository URL. The Action's job summary ends with the line 'Tested with x402-conformance vX.Y.Z' and links the repository. (5) CITATION.cff names Ryan Gillespie and Optitransfer. (6) The 'Add or update my row' form (XC-94, XC-96) has required consent checkboxes covering listing, the CC BY 4.0 data licence with the badge and attribution terms, and testnet-only probes. Nothing in the repository claims endorsement by the x402 Foundation, Coinbase or any vendor, and the x402 logo is not used.

tasks.title: Opt-in matrix: projects add their own details (form, schema, validating workflow to a PR), a compact MATRIX.md and a searchable Pages table, an example row, badges, and weekly freshness with release alignment

deadline.from: signed into proofline.json and every depends_on task done

on_lapse: reassign to the next free agent

tasks.description: The matrix is opt-in only. A project is listed, with its results and a badge for its own README, only after it accepts, through the form or a pull request; nothing about a project that has not accepted is committed, and the outreach list stays private. (1) .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/matrix-row.yml, 'Add or update my row', asks for public details only: project name, type (facilitator self-hosted or hosted, SDK, merchant or paid API, client or wallet, MCP tool), repository URL, docs or site URL, languages, chain families, networks as CAIP-2 ids, environments offered (testnet, devnet, mainnet-only), a testnet endpoint if any, version or commit, optional evidence JSON from the project's own run, a public contact handle (no emails), and three required consents: listing, the CC BY 4.0 licence for public results with the badge terms, and testnet-only probes. (2) matrix/schema/row.schema.json (JSON Schema 2020-12) defines matrix/rows/<slug>.json. tools/matrix_rows.py --from-issue parses the issue, validates it against the schema and the public-safe rules (all three consents, no email address, nothing that looks like a key or mnemonic, https links only, a public handle, a slug no other issue owns) and writes the row; pasted evidence goes through tools/row_from_evidence.py, so the same refusals apply. .github/workflows/matrix-row.yml runs on the issue, passes the untrusted body to the tool only as a file, labels the issue 'matrix-row: valid' or 'matrix-row: needs changes' with a comment saying what to fix, and on a valid issue opens or updates a pull request adding or updating matrix/rows/<slug>.json for maintainer review. Nothing merges automatically and no endpoint is probed from the workflow. (3) The Action's evidence bundle (XC-94) is the evidence: its run.json can be pasted into the form or submitted in a PR. (4) tools/matrix_rows.py --write generates, from matrix/rows/*.json and the committed evidence: the compact listed-projects section of docs/MATRIX.md (a coverage summary of accepted projects by type, chain, language and environment, and the accepted projects with evidence), the full searchable table on the Pages site (docs/site/matrix/index.html and rows.json, CC BY 4.0, one anchor per row for the badge link), and the badges; --check fails when any of them is stale or hand-edited, a row breaks the schema or the rules, consented evidence has no row, or the slug 'example' is used. Every row and the top of docs/MATRIX.md link the form. (5) One example row, labelled 'Example (illustrative, not a real result)', for the placeholder example-org/example-x402-server, shows the format in docs/MATRIX.md and on Pages: example counts, environment, version, release alignment, last run, the evidence link format and the badge markdown; it is never counted in the coverage summary. (6) Listed projects add the badge to their repository: it reads 'Tested with x402-conformance · Optitransfer' and the version tested, links to the project's row, and turns grey with 'stale' when the row is stale; copy-paste Markdown and HTML are given per row. No 'certified', no x402 logo, no endorsement claim. (7) Freshness: docs/templates/x402-conformance.yml is a workflow for a project's own repository (saved as .github/workflows/x402-conformance.yml) that runs the Action with evidence mode on push to the default branch, on release or tag, and weekly. .github/workflows/matrix-freshness.yml runs tools/matrix_freshness.py weekly: through the GitHub API only it records each listed project's latest release or tag and default-branch commit in the row's release field, pulls the evidence artifact from the project's newest successful x402-conformance run through tools/row_from_evidence.py, and opens a pull request for review. A release-alignment column shows 'current' (version tested is the latest release), 'behind (vX tested, vY latest)' or 'stale' (no run within 30 days of the last release check, or behind for 30 days or more), computed from committed dates only so the output is reproducible. (8) Amends where results appear: the named hosted-facilitator list and the self-hosted columns in docs/MATRIX.md are removed until each project accepts; XC-51's self-hosted runs publish the same way, through an accepted row, and docs/MATRIX.md keeps the operator-permission rule for hosted facilitators (XC-M2). Counts only, public-safe, opt-in only.
tasks.evidence_required: The merged PR, the CI run on main where every criterion passes, and the committed evidence named in the criteria. No link, no done.

criteria.statement: The form has every field listed in the description, asks for a public handle and no email, and has three required consent checkboxes (listing, CC BY 4.0 public results with the badge terms, testnet-only probes)

verifier.cmd: f=.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/matrix-row.yml && for k in project type repo site languages chains networks environments endpoint version evidence contact consent; do grep -Eq "id: *$k\b" $f || { echo missing $k; exit 1; }; done && grep -q 'labels: \[matrix-row\]' $f && grep -qi 'no emails' $f && test $(grep -A16 -E 'id: *consent' $f | grep -c 'required: true') -ge 3 && grep -q 'list this project' $f && grep -q 'CC BY 4.0' $f && grep -q 'testnet-only probes' $f

criteria.statement: matrix/schema/row.schema.json is a JSON Schema 2020-12 that requires the three consents as true, a CAIP-2 network list, a handle-shaped contact and an https repo, and allows no other properties

verifier.cmd: python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(open('matrix/schema/row.schema.json'));p=d['properties'];ok=d[chr(36)+'schema'].endswith('2020-12/schema') and d.get('additionalProperties') is False and all(p['consent']['properties'][k].get('const') is True for k in ('listing','data_license','testnet_only')) and 'contact' in d['required'] and 'networks' in d['required'];sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)"

stop_rules: If a criterion cannot pass, STOP and report what blocks it, what was tried and what is needed. Never weaken a criterion, skip a test or raise a timeout to make it pass.

Opt-in only: nothing about a project is committed (no row, no name in a table, no evidence, no badge) until it accepts through the 'Add or update my row' form or a pull request, with the consent recorded there. The outreach list is private and never committed. If a criterion seems to need a row for a project that has not accepted, STOP and report.

Testnet only: never use a mainnet CAIP-2 id as a payment target, never fund a key with anything but testnet faucet tokens, never call a hosted facilitator; every facilitator under test is the loopback double or my own instance on 127.0.0.1.
No auto-merge, ever: the workflows open pull requests for review and never merge, approve or force-push. The untrusted issue body reaches the tool only as a file.

A failing third-party result is reported to that project privately first (SECURITY.md); until the window clears its row shows the failed count and 'under disclosure', with no per-check detail. If a criterion would need that detail to pass, STOP and report.
